headlines.title: Government‑Backed Prestwick Expansion Might Change The Case For Investing In General Electric (GE)
headlines.summary: General Electric recently secured up to £33 million from UK, Scottish and local governments, alongside £27 million of its own investment, to expand its Prestwick jet‑engine maintenance facility, protecting 850 jobs and adding 150 new roles. This government-backed expansion underlines the importance of GE’s UK maintenance hub, which services roughly half of all GE engines on Boeing’s 787, to its broader aerospace operations.

headlines.title: General Electric (GE) Wins UK Backing To Expand Prestwick Jet Engine Jobs
headlines.summary: General Electric (NYSE:GE) secured multi tier UK government funding to protect and expand jet engine maintenance work at its Prestwick site. UK, Scottish and local authorities are committing significant public capital to support jobs tied to GE engines used on Boeing 787 aircraft. GE plans to invest substantial funds to modernize and grow the Prestwick facility as part of a longer term UK footprint.

headlines.title: 3 Big Reasons to Love GE Aerospace (GE)
headlines.summary: GE Aerospace has been treading water for the past six months, recording a small loss of 1.1% while holding steady at $308.37. The stock also fell short of the S&P 500’s 13.5% gain during that period.

headlines.title: GE Aerospace (GE): Can an $11.75B Foundry Deal Defend Its Premium?
headlines.summary: Most companies go shopping when growth starts to fade. GE Aerospace (NYSE:GE) went shopping with revenue still climbing more than 20%. Last month, the jet-engine maker agreed to buy Consolidated Precision Products/CPP, a Cleveland-based maker of superalloy and titanium castings, for $11.75 billion. GE has been a CPP customer for more than 15 years.

headlines.title: Jet engine jobs to stay in UK after taxpayers hand factory £33m
headlines.summary: General Electric (GE) will receive up to £33m of taxpayer funding to stop the US aerospace giant moving jet-engine maintenance jobs out of the UK.

description: General Electric Company, doing business as GE Aerospace, designs and produces commercial and defense aircraft engines, integrated engine components, electric power, and aircraft systems. The company operates through two segments, Commercial Engines & Services, and Defense & Propulsion Technologies. The Commercial Engines & Services segment designs, develops, manufactures, maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) services of jet engines and sale of spare parts for commercial airframes, business aviation, and aeroderivative applications. The Defense & Propulsion Technologies designs, develops, manufactures, and services jet engines and avionics and power systems for governments, militaries, and commercial airframers, as well as MRO of engines and the sale of spare parts. This segment also offers aircraft components and systems, such as small turboprop engines, aeroengine mechanical transmissions, turbines, combustors and controls, additive manufacturing, propeller systems, ignition systems, sensors and engine accessories for fixed wing and rotorcraft applications for commercial and military end users under the Avio Aero, Unison, Dowty Propellers, and Colibrium Additive brands. The company operates in the United States, Europe, Asia, the Americas, the Middle East, and Africa. General Electric Company was incorporated in 1892 and is based in Evendale, Ohio.
